description.narrative:
The EYE 4 SDGs project is a cross-continental initiative empowering youth in Uganda, Kenya, and Belgium to engage in policy advocacy and influence SDG implementation. By identifying gaps in Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)and creating meaningful entry points for youth, the initiative fosters engagement with policymakers to develop inclusive policies that address youth-related challenges. The project aims to assess existing policy gaps and barriers to SDG achievement and empower 400 youth in advocacy,leadership, and policy engagement to strengthen their role in governance. It enhances youth participation in decision-making at local, national, and international levels and promotes collaboration between African and European youth through cross-continental partnerships. Additionally, it encourages intercultural dialogue and exchange programs to share knowledge and experiences while developing policy recommendations that reflect youth perspectives and drive sustainable change.
Aligning with SDGs 3, 4,5, 8, 10, 11, 13, and 17, the project covers key areas such as health, education, gender equality, employment, reduced inequalities, sustainable cities, climate action, and global partnerships. Through capacity-building workshops, advocacy initiatives, andstrategic partnerships, young people gain the knowledge and tools needed to contribute to sustainable development. Activities include conducting gap analysis to evaluate SDG implementation, organizing policy training and leadership programs, hosting intercultural dialogues, creating advocacy strategies, and developing youth-led policy recommendations. Strong communication and dissemination efforts will ensure engagement with civil society,government bodies, and the general public.
The project is expected to increase youth participation in governance and policy advocacy, strengthen collaboration between African and European youth, and develop youth-led policy recommendations with tangible solutions. It will also enhance the visibility and influence ofyouth organizations in SDG implementation and contribute to more inclusive and effective policies on health, education, employment, and sustainability. By equipping young people with skills, knowledge, and platforms, the EYE 4 SDGs Project ensures youth play a central role in shaping a more equitable, sustainable, and inclusive future for all.

participating-org.narrative:
Humanitarian Action for Refugees and Rural Communities Development (HARD Uganda) is a refugee-led, youth and women-driven non-profit organization (RLO). The organization operates in Rhino Camp Extension Omugo and Imvepi Refugee Settlement, Terego District, Uganda, focusing on fostering resilient and self-reliant communities emerging from vulnerability. HARD Uganda was established to address challenges faced by refugees and marginalized host communities lack of education, corruption, mental health struggles, food insecurity, environmental degradation, and economic hardships.
Our Vision: Empowered communities that promote self-reliance, eliminate corruption and discrimination and ensure equality, sustainable development, and peaceful coexistence throughfair resource sharing.
Our Mission: To actively involve and include vulnerable and marginalized individuals in rights-based, sustainable services that build resilience, independence, and opportunities for women, youth, and persons with disabilities.
Our Core Values - Participation and Commitment. - Integrity. - Transparency and Accountability. - Impartiality. - Safety and Dignity.
Objectives: To promote social cohesion and development in the vulnerable communities through involvement and inclusion of individuals for services to pave resilience andindependence of the society’s population.
Working Areas: - SDG Goal 16: Peace, Justice and strong institution <(>&<)> SDG 5 achieve Gender equality and empower all women and girls. - SDG Goal 13: Climate Action - SDG Goal 4: Quality Education - SDG Goal 3: Good Health and Well-being - SDG Goal 1: No Poverty <(>&<)> Goal 8: Decent Work and Economic Growth
